title: Pasta alla Norma
subtitle: Sicilian pasta with aubergine and tomato
excerpt: Fried aubergine, rich tomato sauce and salty aged cheese make this one of Sicily's great pasta dishes. The aubergine should be properly browned and a little crisp at the edges -- not soft and oily. Named after the opera 'Norma' by Catania-born Bellini.
sourceNotes: Pasta alla Norma is from Catania in Sicily. The authentic version uses ricotta salata -- a firm, salty, aged ricotta -- as the finishing cheese.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The tomato sauce can be made a day ahead. Fry the aubergine fresh on the day.

content.text: Salt the aubergine slices before frying. This removes water so they fry rather than steam. Pat them completely dry before they go into the oil.

items.prepNote: use salted ricotta (ricotta salata) -- or crumble feta over the top
for the aubergine and pasta water

content.text: Sprinkle the aubergine cubes with salt. Leave in a colander for 20 minutes. Rinse and pat very dry with kitchen paper.
Heat 3 tablespoons of oil in a wide frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry the aubergine in batches for 6 to 8 minutes until golden on all sides. Do not crowd the pan. Drain on kitchen paper.

In the same pan, add the remaining oil over medium heat. Fry the garlic for 1 minute until golden. Add the tomatoes and crush them with a spoon. Season. Cook for 12 to 15 minutes until the sauce has thickened.
Cook the pasta in well-salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve a mug of pasta water. Drain.
Add the fried aubergine to the tomato sauce. Stir in most of the basil. Toss the pasta through the sauce. Add a splash of pasta water to loosen.
Serve topped with crumbled feta or ricotta salata and the remaining basil leaves.

items.cause: Too much oil, pan not hot enough, or aubergine not dried properly
items.fix: Dry the aubergine thoroughly before frying. Use a hot pan and do not add extra oil. Fry in smaller batches.
Simmer on higher heat, uncovered, until the sauce thickens and darkens slightly.

content.text: Pasta alla Norma is the signature dish of Catania in eastern Sicily. It was supposedly named after the Bellini opera to express how wonderful it was. Ricotta salata is the traditional cheese -- hard, salty and crumbly.
